title: Tiantai
hook: the Chinese school built on the Lotus, founded by Zhiyi

segments.voice: Yesterday we closed the Tibetan traditions: the schools, the stages, mind training, the bardo. Your line was for all beings. When you finished something good, did you pause and let it be for everyone? Today the road turns east again. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-two.

What would you name a school after? Its founder, maybe. Its big idea. Its favorite book. This one carries the name of a mountain. A monk named Zhiyi went up into the hills to teach, and the place stuck to everything he taught there. Students came. Lectures were written down. A whole way of reading the Buddha grew on that slope, and wherever it traveled afterward, it kept the mountain's name. We met Zhiyi once before, sorting a drawer full of sutras. Today we stay with the school itself, and with the one book at its center. Today: Tiantai.
screen: `A SCHOOL NAMED FOR A MOUNTAIN.` → `ZHIYI GOES UP TO TEACH.` → `THE NAME TRAVELS WITH IT.`

segments.voice: First, a new stretch of the path. We've walked through the Tibetan schools. Now come other schools and movements, starting in China, and Tiantai opens the door. Tradition names earlier teachers in its line, but Zhiyi is the one who gave it its shape, and the school is also known by another name: the Lotus school. Second, why the Lotus. This path spent a long stretch inside the Lotus Sutra: the burning house and the carts, the son who wanders off and comes home not knowing he's the heir, the herbs that drink the same rain and grow to different heights, the monk who bows to everyone and says, you will become a Buddha. Zhiyi lectured on that sutra line by line, and on its title, word by word. For Tiantai, the Lotus is where the Buddha finally says the whole of it: all the different paths were one vehicle all along. Third, what that does to everything else. A school built on that reading doesn't need to throw other teachings away. The simpler sutras, the strict rules, the long meditations: Tiantai keeps them, and reads each one as a step toward the same summit. Nothing is wasted. Everything has a place in the one road. Fourth, the school as a way of practice, not only a library. Tiantai joined study and meditation, the book and the cushion, and taught that you need both, the way a bird needs two wings. Over the next days we'll open two of its treasures: a teaching called the three truths, and Zhiyi's practice of stopping and seeing. And later in this stretch we'll watch the school cross the sea to Japan. Today, just the name, and the book underneath it.
screen: `A NEW STRETCH: OTHER SCHOOLS.` · `THE LOTUS AT THE CENTER.` · `NOTHING THROWN AWAY.` · `THE BOOK AND THE CUSHION.` · then, large: `THE LOTUS SCHOOL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: recall the Lotus. Sit, and let a few breaths go by. Then let one picture from the Lotus Sutra come back. The father calling his children out of a burning house. The son working in his own father's yard without knowing it. The rain falling the same on every plant. The monk who bows. Don't pick the best one. Take the one that arrives. Hold it the way you'd hold a photograph, and let the breath keep going underneath it. If your mind wanders, return to the picture. The bell holds the time.
Tiantai. The Chinese school that takes its name from Zhiyi's mountain and reads the whole teaching through the Lotus Sutra. Today's word.
Your line: the Lotus school. Today, when something feels like a detour, try asking where it fits on the road instead of crossing it out. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-two.

howItsDone: Tiantai Buddhists in China, and the Tendai school that grew from it in Japan, study and recite the Lotus Sutra and join that study with meditation.

fork.setup: you hold a stack of sutras that seem to teach different things. you're Zhiyi. what do you do with the simpler ones?
options: keep them, each as a step toward one summit.
fork.reveal: Tiantai keeps them all. for the Lotus school, the many paths turn out to be one vehicle.

original.note: Chinese Tiantai: the name of the mountain where Zhiyi taught, and of his school.

trapdoor: what you thought: Tiantai is a place name.
what it means: a Chinese school honoring Zhiyi as founder, built on the Lotus Sutra, joining study with meditation.
what a scholar hears: the Lotus school, which reads every sutra as a step on one road, because the Lotus says the many vehicles were one.
